extracted.intended_audience: general news readers, consumers interested in fashion/corporate controversies
extracted.subtask_description: News coverage of a retailer's offensive product and the ensuing public backlash, corporate response, and reputational consequences. Focuses on documenting what happened, reactions (consumers, celebrities, advocacy groups), and the company's statements/actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of offensive imagery from online channels
rubrics_metrics.description: H&M: "It has been now removed from all online channels..." (company statement that the image was removed from online channels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate removal of offending images from web/social channels is expected; however, removal of the image alone may be judged insufficient if the product remains available for sale (critics: "They removed the picture but are still selling the item. THAT MAKES IS WORSE").

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceasing sale of the offensive product
rubrics_metrics.description: H&M said "the product will not be for sale in the United States." Consumers demanded the company pull the hoodie from its locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stopping sales (including removing the item from inventory/sites) is a concrete remedial step that stakeholders often expect beyond merely taking down images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public apology and acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: H&M: "We sincerely apologize for this image." The company issued an apology in an email to media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A timely apology is a baseline response; reporting gauges whether the apology appears sincere and is paired with concrete corrective actions (apology alone is often criticized as insufficient).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to internal review and policy/process change
rubrics_metrics.description: H&M: "We believe in diversity and inclusion in all that we do, and will be reviewing our internal routines."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations are expected to promise and undertake internal reviews (e.g., diversity/inclusion procedures, marketing approval processes) to prevent recurrences; reporting notes whether such commitments are specific and actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity to racial/gender stereotypes and slurs in product design
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics noted the hoodie referenced "an insensitive slur used against black people." The article references prior controversies (e.g., Children's Place T-shirt reinforcing gender stereotypes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs and copy should be vetted to avoid reinforcing stereotypes or using language/images that can be construed as racist or sexist; failure to do so is a core cause of backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reaction metrics (social media outrage, boycotts, calls for investigation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The hoodie "sparked a social media backlash, with consumers vowing to stop shopping... and calling for an investigation." Quotes and tweets from users and advocacy groups documented the reaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Severity of backlash is assessed by volume and prominence of responses (consumer boycotts, trending posts, celebrity comments, advocacy group condemnations); these are used to judge reputational impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputational consequences via celebrity/partner disengagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Weeknd said he would no longer be working with H&M after becoming aware of the photo: "i’m deeply offended and will not be working with [H&M] anymore."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loss of celebrity endorsements or partner relationships is a salient indicator of reputational harm and often featured in reporting as an outcome of PR crises.
